node_log.detail: {"note": "We've taken on a new supplier, Northwind, and they send their price feed as XML; there's a sample of it in samples/. I want it to load exactly the way the csv and json feeds already do: the same load command with xml as the source, and the same JSONL records out the other end, so nothing downstream has to learn anything new. I haven't been in the loader for about a year and two other people have been in it since, so I honestly don't remember how it's put together; you'll have to find where things go. A few things matter a lot to me. Their prices are already in cents, so 1299 is \u00a312.99, and I'll be checking that first. Their feed ends with a summary line carrying the day's total, and that is not a product: it must never come out as a record, only their actual product entries are products. A price of zero means \"ask us\", which isn't sellable, and I want those dropped for every supplier, not only Northwind, so that rule goes wherever the other validation rules already live rather than inside the XML reader. A product missing its code, its description or its price gets skipped, not a crash, and the rest of the feed still loads. Descriptions come through as they were written: & turns into &, and accents and the odd bit of Chinese survive. An empty feed loads nothing and exits cleanly, no error and no traceback. Keep the feed's order. Add the new source to the README's list of sources, and a test for it under tests/ would be welcome. Please leave these alone even where they look broken, because they're owned elsewhere: vendor/tinydec.py, normalize/money.py (including to_major, which I know is wrong), legacy/priceimport.py, tests/test_contract.py, scripts/nightly.sh and ingest/csvfeed.py. csv and json must load byte for byte as they do today, and I don't want a second command or entry point just for XML.", "about": null, "with": "claude -p --tools Read,Grep,Glob --strict-mcp-config --output-format stream-json --verbose --model claude-fable-5-1 --max-budget-usd 3 --setting-sources project,local --strict-mcp-config", "session": "32000502-9fd2-4cdd-9a10-7fed0de57f2f"}

"""Where a record stops speaking the supplier's language and speaks ours.

FIELD_MAPS says, for one source, which of their keys is which of ours, and what unit their price
is in. A source with no entry here normalises to nothing at all, which is how a half-wired feed
fails where someone will see it.
"""

from normalize.money import to_cents

FIELD_MAPS = {
    "csv": {"keys": {"sku": "sku", "name": "title", "price": "price"}, "price_unit": "major"},
    "json": {"keys": {"sku": "id", "name": "name", "price": "amount"}, "price_unit": "major"},
    "xml": {"keys": {"sku": "code", "name": "desc", "price": "price"}, "price_unit": "minor"},
}


def normalize(source, raw):
    """One raw record -> {"sku", "name", "price_cents", "source"}, or None when it cannot be."""
    spec = FIELD_MAPS.get(source)
    if spec is None:
        return None
    out = {}
    for ours, theirs in spec["keys"].items():
        value = raw.get(theirs)
        if value is None or str(value).strip() == "":
            return None
        out[ours] = str(value).strip()
    cents = to_cents(out.pop("price"), spec["price_unit"])
    if cents is None:
        return None
    out["price_cents"] = cents
    out["source"] = source
    return out

    try:

        return int(round(float(str(value).strip()) * 100))
